sections.h2: Which way should I sell a Gastonia house?
sections.html:
Gastonia owners can go to market with an agent, find a buyer on their own, or take a cash offer for the house in its present state. Repairs, timing and the amount you will give up for speed decide which is best.

  • A listing reaches the most buyers but asks for prep, showings and an agent's fee.
  • A private sale saves the fee and adds contract work.
  • A cash sale closes on your schedule and skips the repair list, normally for less.

Gastonia has many older houses near the old mill districts, so a cash offer often comes up for homes with deferred work.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Gastonia, and how does it affect houses today?
sections.html:
Gastonia began in 1873 as a small railroad depot and was incorporated in 1877, according to the city's history page. The crossing of the Atlanta and Charlotte Air Line Railroad and a narrow gauge line, together with the steam-powered textile mill, drove early growth.

The same page says the town started with roughly 200 people on less than one square mile, was voted county seat in 1911, and has run under a council-manager government since 1919. It describes Gastonia as the largest of Gaston County's 15 municipalities, with more than 72,000 residents and about 51.99 square miles.

That mill history left a mix of housing ages. Houses built around the textile era tend to have older wiring, plumbing and foundations, which is worth an inspection before you set a price.

sections.h2: How does Gaston County value a house in Gastonia?
sections.html:
Gaston County's tax office values every parcel, and the commissioners voted in 2025 to move to a four-year reappraisal cycle. The county's FAQ says state law requires a reappraisal at least every eight years, so Gaston now does it more often.

A recent county news release says the proposed Schedule of Values was first presented to the commissioners on August 25, with an updated version posted on September 29 and scheduled for adoption at the October 27 meeting. Ask the Gaston County Tax Office whether the schedule was adopted and what your new assessed value is, since that decision is not something to guess.

The county FAQ explains that the tax bill is the tax value divided by 100 and multiplied by the rate, and that the county and cities publish a revenue-neutral rate during the budget cycle. A higher value may or may not mean a higher bill.

sections.h2: When is Gaston County property tax due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Property tax is due September 1, and interest starts on January 6 at 2 percent, then three-fourths of one percent per month. Those terms come from G.S. 105-360, and the Gaston tax collection page repeats the same schedule.

Listing runs from the first business day of January through January 31 under G.S. 105-307. Gaston's personal property page adds a 10 percent late listing penalty for listings not filed in that period.

sections.h2: Can a Gastonia owner who is 65 or disabled get a lower tax bill?
sections.html:
Possibly. The state sets three relief programs and an owner can use only one, with applications going to the county assessor on Form AV-9. The elderly or disabled exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1 removes the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value of the permanent residence.

  • The owner must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, as of January 1.
  • Income must fall at or under the limit, printed by the state as $38,800 for 2026.
  • The disabled veteran exclusion, a separate program, removes the first $45,000 of value.

Ask the Gaston County assessor which program fits and what deadline applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Gastonia house?
sections.html:
A small estate can be collected by affidavit rather than a full administration. G.S. 28A-25-1 sets the limit for an intestate estate at $20,000 in personal property after liens, usable once 30 days have passed since the death.

  • A surviving spouse who is the sole heir may use a higher cap, up to $30,000 after spousal allowance.
  • The affidavit is filed with the clerk of superior court where the decedent lived.
  • The statute asks for a description of each tract of real property owned.

A house counts as real property, so ask an estate attorney or the clerk who may sign the deed before you accept any offer.

sections.h2: Where does a Gastonia sale get recorded and who handles the courthouse side?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the Gaston County register of deeds, and the closing attorney normally handles the filing and the fees on your settlement statement. Ask for that statement in writing before the closing date so you can see every line.

The city's history page adds a note on the courthouse. Gastonia won the county seat vote in 1911, and the county's former courthouse on South Street, later restored and dedicated as the James B. Garland Municipal Business Center in 2002, shows how long county business has centered here. The current courthouse opened June 15, 1998 at North Marietta Street and Long Avenue.

If you need court filings tied to a sale, such as an estate matter or a lien payoff, those filings go to the Gaston County courthouse, so plan a trip or ask your attorney to file for you.

faqs.q: Is Gastonia the county seat of Gaston County?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's history page says Gastonia was voted county seat in 1911.

faqs.q: How often does Gaston County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Every four years, after the commissioners adopted that cycle in 2025, per the county's FAQ.
The Gaston County register of deeds, usually through the closing attorney handling the sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gastonia house I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, once you have legal authority to sign. A small estate may use the affidavit process in G.S. 28A-25-1, but ask the clerk of superior court which route applies.

faqs.q: When does interest start on unpaid Gaston County tax?
faqs.a: On January 6, at 2 percent, then three-fourths of one percent per month, per G.S. 105-360.
